subsystems.name: Core Format API
subsystems.description: Core Format API is the type-erased argument and buffered-output foundation that fmt's formatting entry points build on. It exists as a separate unit because the library needs one stable place to hold the polymorphic value model, format-spec parsing state, and output buffers that all higher-level formatters can reuse, so a formatter written for a custom type does not have to know whether output goes to a string, a container, or a FILE*. Control starts when format() packages arguments; dynamic_arg_list (include/fmt/args.h:43) and named_arg_store (include/fmt/base.h:2326) manage runtime and named arguments, while parse_context (include/fmt/base.h:842) tracks argument ids and buffer (include/fmt/base.h:1759) receives rendered chunks. The format engine then calls basic_format_arg::get or visit (include/fmt/base.h:2545 / :2504) to dispatch to a type's formatter; in compile mode compile_format_string (include/fmt/compile.h:385) turns the format string into a typed structure before rendering. It connects to chrono.h, color.h, ranges.h, std.h, and xchar.h, which add formatter specializations and wide-string entry points on top of this core.

subsystems.name: Chrono Stream Support
subsystems.description: This subsystem adapts std::chrono and std::ostream types to fmt's formatter protocol. It is separated from the core so the complexity of calendar arithmetic, locale-specific tm fields, and stream insertion is isolated behind formatter specializations, keeping the central format engine independent of std::chrono headers. For chrono values, parse_chrono_format (include/fmt/chrono.h:630) validates the spec, tm_writer (include/fmt/chrono.h:1044) emits date and time fields, and duration_formatter (include/fmt/chrono.h:1612) combines safe_duration_cast (include/fmt/chrono.h:160) with fractional-second handling to render durations. For ostreams, format() wraps a type via streamed (include/fmt/ostream.h:114), and formatter<detail::streamed_view<T>, Char> (include/fmt/ostream.h:96) funnels the value into write_buffer (include/fmt/ostream.h:55). std.h builds related standard-library formatters, such as formatter<std::optional<T>> (include/fmt/std.h:400), on the same interface. It depends on format.h for core formatter machinery and interoperates with xchar.h for wide-character formatting.

subsystems.name: Extended Format Features
subsystems.description: This subsystem contains the optional front-end formatters that make fmt convenient: ANSI terminal styling, range/tuple/container formatting, and wide-character entry points. It is a separate unit so users pay compile-time cost only for features they opt into, and because these features are orthogonal to the core value and argument machinery in format.h. Color output begins with text_style (include/fmt/color.h:236), which stores foreground, background, and emphasis, and ansi_color_escape (include/fmt/color.h:366) translates it to escape sequences before formatter<detail::styled_arg<T>, Char> (include/fmt/color.h:620) renders the wrapped value. ranges.h classifies containers with range_format_kind_ (include/fmt/ranges.h:253), then dispatches to map, string, sequence, tuple, or join formatter specializations such as the sequence formatter at include/fmt/ranges.h:501; xchar.h wraps all the core entry points for wchar_t, e.g. make_wformat_args (include/fmt/xchar.h:126). It connects to format.h for the core API and to ostream.h for stream-friendly print helpers.

subsystems.name: Format Engine Implementation
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the compiled, non-header-only part of the library: src/fmt.cc conditionally builds fmt as a C++ module, src/format.cc is the companion implementation translation unit, and src/os.cc supplies POSIX and Windows file-descriptor plumbing used by file and buffered_file. It exists because many of fmt's formatting primitives are templates, but a few operations such as error messaging, file I/O, and module export glue must live in exactly one translation unit and be exported from the library ABI. The module unit src/fmt.cc establishes FMT_MODULE (src/fmt.cc:10) and FMT_EXPORT (src/fmt.cc:108), deciding what is visible; src/os.cc then provides concrete helpers such as system_message (src/os.cc:75), file (src/os.cc:216), and pipe (src/os.cc:342) that the header include/fmt/os.h declares. This keeps header-only users unaffected while linked users get those symbols from the compiled artifact. It connects to test/posix-mock-test.cc, which exercises the same OS layer with mock POSIX calls.

subsystems.name: Documentation Scripts
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the documentation site's client-side JavaScript, responsible for the dynamic parts of the fmt manual that static HTML cannot provide. It exists as a separate unit to keep C++ header documentation content and website behavior independent, so documentation changes do not require recompiling the library. On page load, doc/fmt.js hooks into document elements and enhances them; the scan found no function or class symbols, so its behavior is loaded directly as a script rather than through an exported API. It has no related files in this build, meaning it is self-contained and does not participate in the library's format engine or build graph.

subsystems.name: C Wrapper Header
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the C wrapper header for {fmt}, exposing a small set of plain-C functions that convert C scalar and string values into C++ format arguments. It exists as a separate unit to give C programs a stable C ABI and a header that does not require a C++ compiler, while still routing through the C++ formatting engine. A C caller uses fmt_from_int, fmt_from_uint, fmt_from_bool, fmt_from_char, fmt_from_float, fmt_from_double, fmt_from_long_double, fmt_from_str, and fmt_from_ptr to build argument lists that are then consumed by the implementation in src/fmt-c.cc. The repeated FMT_CAPI definitions at include/fmt/fmt-c.h:17 choose the correct import/export decoration for shared libraries on different platforms. The header connects directly to src/fmt-c.cc, which implements the declared functions, while staying independent of the C++ core API so downstream C projects can include only this one file. Since no related files were recorded, its main coupling is to the wrapper implementation and to any consumer that installs the published C header.

subsystems.description: This subsystem implements the C wrapper functions declared in include/fmt/fmt-c.h and is the bridge that converts C-style variadic argument lists into fmt's type-safe format_args by calling convert_c_format_args at src/fmt-c.cc:14. It exists as a separate translation unit so all C++ exception handling and template instantiation stay out of the public C header and are compiled once into the fmt library. The FMT_CATCH macro wraps the exported bodies at src/fmt-c.cc:50 and src/fmt-c.cc:65, converting C++ exceptions into an error result for C callers. Data flows from a C caller's va_list into format_args via convert_c_format_args, then into fmt_vformat or fmt_vprint at src/fmt-c.cc:38 and src/fmt-c.cc:54, with the formatted result returned as a string or written to stdout. Because no related files were recorded, the main neighboring subsystem is the header itself; the implementation also depends on the core fmt formatting engine whose entry points are referenced inside these functions.

subsystems.name: Build Support Scripts
subsystems.description: This file is a vendored copy of the docopt command-line argument parser, used by the repository's build and support scripts to turn usage-message docstrings into parsed options. It exists as a separate utility so all Python tooling shares one dependency-free implementation rather than relying on an external package. Entry point docopt at support/docopt.py:490 parses the usage pattern through parse_expr, parse_seq, parse_atom, and parse_shorts/parse_long into a Pattern tree, then calls Pattern.match to decide whether argv satisfies it. The tree is normalized first by fix_identities and fix_repeating_arguments, and token handling is encapsulated by the Tokens class at support/docopt.py:282. The different node classes Required, Optional, OneOrMore, and Either encode how matches are combined at support/docopt.py:219, support/docopt.py:232, support/docopt.py:246, and support/docopt.py:268. This subsystem connects to build scripts by providing their CLI contract; since no related files were recorded, its only links are the scripts that import it and the usage strings they pass into docopt.

subsystems.name: Unicode Utility Script
subsystems.description: This script generates the printable-characters table used by {fmt} from Python's Unicode database. It exists as a separate support utility so the C++ source tables can be regenerated when the Unicode version changes, instead of maintaining large code-point lists by hand. main at support/printable.py:133 coordinates the pipeline: get_file fetches or opens the Unicode data file, get_codepoints enumerates code points and classifies them, compress_singletons and compress_normal turn the set into compact singleton and range forms, and print_singletons/print_normal emit the generated tables. Helper functions to_ranges and get_escaped at support/printable.py:18 and support/printable.py:30 convert individual code points into ranges and escaped character literals. The script is invoked from a developer's shell or build script, and the text it prints is copied into fmt source files that drive printable-character checks. Since no related files were recorded, its interface is the generated output plus the command-line inputs handled by main.

subsystems.name: Docstrings Handler
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the mkdocstrings C++ handler that turns Doxygen XML for {fmt} into HTML/Markdown documentation for the project's documentation site. It exists as a separate Python package under support/python so the documentation generator can import one handler without coupling to the fmt C++ codebase. The pipeline starts with Definition at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:24 wrapping each XML node, then collect_compound and collect at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:313 and support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:358 walk the Doxygen tree and accumulate members. Rendering is driven by render_decl and render at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:181 and support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:423, which use convert_template_params, convert_type, convert_params, and convert_return_type to produce type strings, while doxyxml2html and tag_map handle markup. CxxHandler.__init__ at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:236 stores collected data, and get_handler at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:447 registers the plugin with mkdocstrings. This handler connects Doxygen XML generated from fmt's C++ headers to the mkdocstrings/MkDocs pipeline, importing the mkdocstrings base classes that define the plugin interface.

subsystems.name: Release Automation
subsystems.description: Release Automation provides a thin Python wrapper around Git operations and shell command execution used to prepare clean build and documentation environments. The Git class (support/release.py:19) turns subprocess calls into reusable methods such as clone, fetch, pull, commit, and push, while Runner (support/release.py:69) executes arbitrary commands in a controlled manner. It exists as a separate unit to isolate the messy, side-effecting parts of release tooling, such as checkout, reset, and environment creation, from the rest of the repository so release logic can be reused and tested without leaking subprocess machinery into callers. Control flows from create_build_env (support/release.py:81) and create_doc_env (support/release.py:92), which first call clean_checkout (support/release.py:60) to reset a repository, and then use Runner/Git to set up environments and push artifacts. The module keeps repository state reproducible by using clean_checkout to force a known state before any build or documentation generation begins. Its related_files list is empty, so it currently has no direct coupling to other scanned subsystems; instead it acts as a standalone support module whose only external connections are to the system git executable and the shell environment.

files.role: Central support module for release automation. It defines wrappers for Git and command execution plus environment-creation helpers, so release jobs can invoke safe, repeatable operations without embedding subprocess calls in every script. This file is the only file in the subsystem and exposes the high-level entry points used by release workflows.

overview.description: This repository is the {fmt} formatting library, a C++ text-formatting system built around a type-erased core API that packages arguments, parses format specs, and writes rendered output to buffers or streams. The Core Format API provides the foundational polymorphic value model and output infrastructure, while the Chrono Stream Support and Extended Format Features layers supply optional formatter specializations for chrono types, ostreams, ANSI colors, ranges, and wide characters. A compiled Format Engine Implementation supplies the non-template ABI pieces such as error messaging and file-descriptor helpers, and separate C wrapper header/implementation expose a plain-C interface for C callers. Supporting the library are documentation and release tooling: Documentation Scripts enrich the manual, the Docstrings Handler converts Doxygen XML for the docs site, Release Automation manages build/doc environments, and Unicode Utility and Build Support Scripts generate tables and parse CLI options. All subsystems either build on the core formatting machinery or support its maintenance and distribution, with the core's buffer and argument interfaces tying the higher-level formatters and C bridge together.
